svg.title: Unstage a file, keep your edits.
svg.desc: Git 2.23 or newer, inside a repository with at least one commit. In this example note.txt held hello in the last commit. The working file was edited and saved with an added again line, then staged with git add note.txt. The staging area holds the file versions selected for the next commit. git restore --staged note.txt replaces only the staged version with the last committed version. A before and after diagram shows the last commit unchanged, staging returning to hello, and the working file retaining hello and again. git diff --cached -- note.txt inspects the staged difference before and after: the added line before, no difference afterward. These are illustrative file contents, not terminal output.
svg.text: UNSTAGE A FILE, KEEP YOUR EDITS.
Staging holds file versions selected for the next commit (saved snapshot).
Requires Git 2.23+; inside a repository with at least one commit.
Independent example: committed note.txt held hello; its saved file now adds again.
After git add note.txt, unstage restores staging from the last commit; keep your edits.
Example note.txt contents. Working file = saved file you edit.
Inspect: git diff --cached -- note.txt — added line before; no difference after.
